newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Spread trades executed in FTSE options.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Spread trades executed in FTSE options.

text.p: The larger trades in UK equity options on Tuesday were in the FTSE 100 index, dealers said.
The main trade by mid-afternoon was a bear spread established by selling 1,000 March 4250 calls and buying 1,000 March 4300 calls for a net credit of 20-1/2p.
A maximum profit of 20-1/2p will be made at expiry if the index stays below 4250.
In another deal a calendar spread was bought and it involved selling 250 February 4250 calls and buying 250 March 4250 calls for a net debit of 25p.
In general, the effect of options time decay will be that the spread will widen to its maximum value if the FTSE is 4250 at February expiry.
The position may then be closed to capture the resultant profit, or the long March calls held in order to make more money if the index subsequently goes up.
In two further large deals there was a seller of 1,000 June 3300 puts at 8p and a buyer who traded at the same price.
By 1510 GMT, the FTSE index was up 19.3 at 4231.3.
Over in stock options British Telecommunications were active as traders bought put options.
One such deal was the purchase of 1,000 May 390 puts at 6p.
BT shares added a penny to 424p.
Also in the telephone networks sector, the main trade in mobile telephone group Orange was the sale of 500 March 200 calls at prices of 14p and 16p. The shares fell 5p on profit-taking to 209p.
Elsewhere, in pay television broadcasting company British Sky Broadcasting Group one trader bought 325 June 650 calls at 19p.The shares added 16p to 580p.
